title: Possessive adjectives
rule: Before the noun: mi(s), tu(s), su(s), nuestro/a(s), vuestro/a(s), su(s).
They agree with the thing owned, not the owner: mis libros (my books), nuestra casa (our house).
su / sus can mean his, her, its, your (usted/ustedes) or their.
After the noun or alone: mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro… (un amigo mío, Este libro es mío).

questions: Ana y Luis visitan a ___ abuela.
Ese bolígrafo no es tuyo, es ___.
Alone after ser, and bolígrafo is masculine: mío.
After the noun the long form is used, agreeing with amiga: mía.
Talking to María (tú), before the noun: tu.
Estas gafas no son mías, son ___.
Alone, agreeing with gafas (feminine plural): suyas.
